niche.title: California MEXICAN Judge INDICTED in $2M Bribery Case, Faces Up to 135 YEARS in Prison!
niche.description:
A shocking arrest has taken place in Colombia, targeting a Mexican federal judge. The U.S. Department of Justice alleges that Luis Benitez Alcantarra pocketed $2 million in bribes—in exchange for which he issued an order to release Andrew Clark, a top lieutenant to former Olympian Ryan Wedding.
Notably, the massive payment and the release order occurred on the very same day. While the judge is currently presumed innocent, these remarkably well-aligned circumstances have drawn intense public scrutiny. So, what exactly transpired on that fateful day?
In 2002, Ryan Wedding was a Winter Olympian.

outliers.title: The FBI Agent Who Googled Himself (Sort Of) #spy #fbi #coldwar #shorts
outliers.description:
From 1998 on, an FBI agent kept typing his own name into the FBI's case system. His own street, too, and "dead drop and Washington".

Robert Hanssen sold America's secrets to Moscow, on and off, for more than twenty years. He hacked the bureau's network and reported it as a security flaw, left packages under footbridges in Virginia parks, and never told his KGB handlers his name. The FBI hunted the wrong man for years, until a KGB file with his fingerprints and his voice in it gave him away. Then it promoted him, into computer security, to keep an eye on him.
